lines.t: This one useless option makes you spend more money. And you've fallen for it.
lines.title: THE *USELESS* OPTION

lines.t: A magazine offered three subscriptions. Online only, fifty-nine dollars. Print only, one hundred twenty-five. Print plus online… also one hundred twenty-five.
Nobody picks print only. That's the point. It's a decoy.
When behavioral economist Dan Ariely tested it on MIT students, eighty-four percent chose the expensive combo.
lines.title: CHOSE THE *$125* COMBO

lines.t: Remove the decoy… and only thirty-two percent did. Most switched to the cheap option.
lines.title: WHO CHOSE THE *COMBO*

lines.t: Next time you see a weird middle option, ask yourself: who is that option really for?
lines.title: SPOT THE *DECOY*
